question: A 1 cm line is made of points, each of length zero. How can the zeros add up to 1 cm?
options: Each point has a tiny non-zero length
The line's true length is zero
Length adds only over countable collections
answer: Length adds only over countable collections. Measure theory adds lengths over sets that can be listed one by one; a line's points cannot. Adolf Grünbaum used this in 1967 against Zeno's claim that a line of sizeless parts has no size. All the fractions between 0 and 1, taken together, have length zero.
move: When parts cannot add to the whole, question the adding, not the parts.
trap: Rescuing the sum by giving each point a sliver of length.
source: Grünbaum, Modern Science and Zeno's Paradoxes, 1967
reference: Grünbaum, Modern Science and Zeno's Paradoxes, Wesleyan University Press, 1967
